gemini-argon-R1.change: Remediation on `p20/remediation-r1` from F: `pause_reclaim_victim` returns false once a failed `pause_resident` leaves `checkpoints_.pending()`/an export in flight (no older resident paused); `reserve_resident_units` waits (stop/break) on pending saves/exports after a failed pause instead of throwing; same-class sweep of engine_core.h; red→green EngineCore regression (Host durable victim + Pending handler + two residents + Device KV shortage).
gemini-argon-R1.rationale: Lead traced the chain at F: `approve_release` → `allow_release` (context_cache/resource_manager.h:1680-1694) → release guard → `checkpoint_pressure` (engine_checkpoint.inl:547-560) → `CheckpointControl::settle` sets `pending_progress_` and returns false for a Pending save (checkpoint_control.h:154-175); `pause_reclaim_victim` then tries older residents (engine_core.h:1844-1853) and `reserve_resident_units` throws at 2356 because its only pending check (2344) precedes the pause. The guard is enabled whenever a pressure-checkpoint handler is installed (engine_checkpoint.inl:20-21), i.e. on the shipped durable-session profile. Same shape exists in shipped a87de361 (`oldest resident cannot obtain its legal unit`), but F rotates the pressure owner and pauses more often under sustained C2 pressure. Consequence is an Engine-wide failure of active/paused/waiting requests: P1 after controls.

claude-mythos-U1.rationale: Answered from vendored/bound source: `listen_internal()` calls `task_queue->shutdown()` before returning (httplib.h:13739); the fork queue `HttpTaskQueue::shutdown` → `TaskPool::shutdown` joins workers (src/core/cpu/task_pool.cpp:33-41) whose loop exits only when `queued == 0` (48-67), so every queued and active handler completes before `listen_after_bind()` returns and `final_save()` runs (http_server.cpp:705-707). No late-publication window.

daybreak-blue-R1.change: Same remediation branch: `Scheduler::take_fresh_window()` consumes the window (`rotations_since_fresh_ = 0`) when it returns true, so an unsuccessful or skipped window cannot reopen before a complete service rotation; red→green test_scheduler regression (≥3 members, window taken and ended without admission, next owner served, no window until a complete rotation). Duplicate of gpt-astra-R1 (one root cause).
daybreak-blue-R1.rationale: Verified at F: scheduler.h:238 resets `rotations_since_fresh_` only inside `admitted()`; scheduler.h:297 reopens `fresh_window_` whenever the counter is still ≥ membership; engine_core.h:2744-2757 takes and ends the window regardless of `try_admit_one(false)` success. The maintainer contract (resource-scheduling-and-context-cache.md:442-446) bounds fresh windows to one per complete rotation including an unsuccessful attempt. Impact is repeated catalog-only admission/reclaim planning per quantum (interference, possible avoidable catalog eviction), no preemption: P2.

gpt-astra-R1.change: Merged with daybreak-blue-R1 (same root cause and change).
gpt-astra-R1.rationale: Supplemental lane; identical root cause verified by the lead (scheduler.h:238/297, engine_core.h:2744-2757).

claude-mythos-R1.rationale: Premise false for the vendored cpp-httplib: `Server::stop()` exchanges and closes `svr_sock_` unconditionally (third_party/cpp-httplib/httplib.h:13056-13066), and `listen_internal()` returns false without serving when the socket is already invalid (13657-13660). A stop landing between `HttpServer::listen()`’s check and `listen_after_bind()` therefore makes listen return; `final_save` still runs (src/serve/http_server.cpp:705-707) and main exits. No hang.
